transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I suppose… it’s become a bit ridiculous at home. I keep avoiding parts of the house because I might see spiders. The basement laundry gets left, I won’t go into the garden shed, and I’ve even paid people to do small jobs I could do myself, just so I don’t have to go in those places.
Do you experience panic or intense fear when you encounter or even think about being in those places where spiders might be?
Yes… if I see one, it’s immediate. My chest sort of tightens, my hands shake, and I just… freeze, or I’m backing away before I’ve even really thought about it.
Is your fear or avoidance limited to situations where you might encounter spiders, or are there other things or situations that cause you similar distress?

It’s really just spiders, or places where I think one might be. I know, rationally, one in the corner of an old house probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I imagine one dropping out of a box or being near the washer, it just feels… much bigger and more threatening than it should. It’s embarrassing.
Does thinking about spiders when you're not in a situation where you might encounter them also cause you significant distress?

Yes… sometimes. Not all the time, but if I picture one, like dropping out of a box or sitting near the washer, it feels much bigger and more threatening than I know it really is. I do know it probably wouldn’t hurt me, but… it still gets to me.
Is your fear of spiders the same no matter where you might encounter them, or is it worse in certain situations or places?

It’s worse in certain places. Mostly the basement, the garden shed… places like that. I’ve found myself putting off laundry or paying someone to do little jobs I could do myself, just so I don’t have to go in there and possibly see one.
Is your fear of spiders ever triggered by something other than actually seeing a spider or thinking you might see one, such as a picture or a story about spiders?

Yes… pictures can do it sometimes, or even just someone talking about them. It’s not as bad as seeing one, but if I start picturing one dropping out of a box or sitting near the washer, it suddenly feels… huge, threatening. I know that sounds silly, but it does.
Has your fear of spiders affected your relationships or work in any way?

Work, not much… I manage there. But at home, yes, it’s made things harder. I put off chores in certain parts of the house, and I’ve paid people to do small maintenance things I probably should be able to handle myself. It’s… made owning the house more expensive and a bit more stressful.
Is there anything else about spiders or the situations where you might encounter them that frightens you, beyond just their presence?

Yes… I suppose it’s the way I imagine them appearing suddenly. I know a spider in the corner of an old house probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I picture one dropping out of a box or being by the washer, it feels… much bigger and more threatening than it should. I’m a bit embarrassed by that.
Is your fear of spiders ever less intense if you know you will be with someone else when you are in a place where spiders might be present?
I’m not sure, really. Maybe a little, if someone else is there… but I haven’t paid close attention to that. It’s still uncomfortable either way.
Is your fear of spiders only about the spiders themselves, or is it also about the possibility of encountering them in certain situations or environments?

It’s… not only the spider itself. It’s more the thought of where it might turn up — like if I open a box, or go near the washer, and suddenly it’s there. I know it’s probably not dangerous, but in that moment it feels much bigger than it is. I feel a bit silly saying that.
Is your fear of spiders ever triggered by thinking about being in a specific place where spiders might be, even if you don't actually see one?

Yes… it can be just thinking about a place. Like if I imagine opening an old box, or going near the washer, and there might be one there. Even if I don’t see anything, I start picturing it dropping out or sitting there, and it feels much more threatening than it probably is. It’s embarrassing, really.
Is your fear of spiders ever triggered by thinking about the context or situation in which you might encounter a spider, rather than the spider itself?

Yes… it’s often the situation, I suppose. I know a spider in the corner of some old house probably wouldn’t hurt me, but if I picture one dropping out of a box or sitting near the washer, it suddenly feels… much bigger, more threatening than it should. I’m a bit embarrassed by that.
Is your fear of spiders ever triggered by the thought of being in a situation where you can't easily escape if you encounter a spider?

Yes… I think so. It’s not just the spider, exactly. If I imagine one dropping out of a box or being near the washer, and I’d have to get past it, it feels… enormous, much more threatening than it probably is. I know that sounds a bit silly.
Is your fear of spiders ever triggered by the thought of the spider itself, without considering where or how you might encounter it?

Not usually just the spider by itself, no. It’s more when I imagine it suddenly being somewhere near me… like dropping out of a box or being by the washer. Then it feels much bigger and more threatening than I know it really is. I’m a bit embarrassed saying that.
Is your fear ever of the place itself where spiders might be, rather than just the spiders?

A little, yes… but it’s more what I imagine happening there. Like, an old house is probably fine, and a spider in a corner won’t hurt me. But if I picture one falling out of a box, or being near the washer, it suddenly feels much more threatening than it should. I don’t really like admitting that.
Is your fear only of spiders themselves or also of the situations or contexts in which you might encounter them?

It’s… not only the spider, I suppose. I know if there’s one in the corner of an old house, it probably won’t hurt me. But if I picture it dropping out of a box, or sitting near the washer, it suddenly feels much bigger and more threatening than it really is. I’m a bit embarrassed by that.
Do you experience similar intense fears or avoidance behaviors with things other than spiders?
Not really… I can’t think of anything else that’s quite like that. It’s mainly the spiders.
Is your fear of spiders also about what might happen if you were to touch or be touched by one, rather than just seeing it?

Yes… sort of. It’s not just seeing it. If I imagine one dropping out of a box or being near the washer and somehow getting on me, it feels… much bigger and more threatening than it really is. I know that sounds silly, and I’m embarrassed by it.
